stories.headline: SpaceX exercises option to buy AI coding startup Cursor for $60B all-stock

key_facts.fact: SpaceX signed a binding agreement to acquire Anysphere (Cursor) in an all-stock deal valuing the company at $60 billion, expected to close in Q3 2026
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX has agreed to acquire AI coding startup Cursor in a $60 billion stock deal, just a few days after the space company's historic IPO... SpaceX said Tuesday that the acquisition is likely to close in the third quarter of this year.

key_facts.fact: The April option gave SpaceX the right to buy Cursor for $60B or pay a $10B break-up fee ($1.5B cash plus $8.5B in computing resources)
key_facts.excerpt: In April, SpaceX said it had obtained the right to acquire Cursor for $60 billion later this year. If, for some reason, the deal is not consummated, SpaceX had agreed to pay Cursor a 'termination fee' of $1.5 billion, and $8.5 billion in computing resources, according to its IPO filings.

key_facts.fact: The $60B in Class A common stock represented 3.4% dilution at SpaceX's IPO valuation
key_facts.excerpt: The $60 billion in class A common stack that SpaceX has agreed to pay to acquire Cursor represented a 3.4% dilution at the aerospace and tech conglomerate's IPO valuation.

key_facts.fact: Cursor was on track to close a $2B round from Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive and Nvidia at a $50B valuation before SpaceX intervened
key_facts.excerpt: The company, founded in 2022 and led by 25-year-old chief executive Michael Truell, was on track to close a $2bn round from Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive and Nvidia at a $50bn valuation before SpaceX intervened.

key_facts.fact: Deal structure: SpaceX subsidiary X67 Inc. merges into Cursor, which survives as a wholly owned subsidiary; Cursor shares convert based on SpaceX's average share price over the seven trading days before close
key_facts.excerpt: A SpaceX subsidiary, X67 Inc., will merge into Cursor, which survives as a wholly owned subsidiary. Cursor's shares convert into SpaceX Class A stock based on an implied equity value of $60bn, priced on the company's average share price over the seven trading days before the deal closes.

key_facts.fact: Acquisition is meant to help SpaceX's AI division (built around the xAI merger earlier this year) close the gap with Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex
key_facts.excerpt: Musk has previously expressed his frustration with xAI's sub-par coding product, which lags behind popular tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex. Acquiring Cursor, which offers similar tools to automate coding, could help close the gap.

stories.headline: Z.ai releases GLM-5.2: 1M-context coding model under MIT license, beats GPT-5.5

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI startup Z.ai (formerly Zhipu) released GLM-5.2, a 753B-parameter open-weights LLM with a stable 1M-token context window, under an unrestricted MIT license
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Chinese AI startup Z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI) announced the immediate release of GLM-5.2, a 753-billion parameter open-weights large language model (LLM) engineered specifically to dominate 'long-horizon' autonomous coding and engineering tasks... z.ai has released GLM-5.2's core weights under an unrestricted MIT open-source license

key_facts.fact: GLM-5.2 trails Anthropic's Opus 4.8 by just 1% on FrontierSWE while outperforming GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 on multiple coding benchmarks, ranking the highest open-source model on FrontierSWE, PostTrainBench, and SWE-Marathon
key_facts.excerpt: Across FrontierSWE, PostTrainBench, and SWE-Marathon, it consistently ranks among the top models overall—trailing Opus 4.8 by just 1% on FrontierSWE, outperforming GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 on multiple benchmarks, and remaining the highest-ranked open-source model across all three.

key_facts.fact: Architecture: mixture-of-experts with ~744-753B total parameters and roughly 40B active per token; the new IndexShare technique reuses one indexer across four sparse-attention layers, cutting per-token FLOPs by 2.9x at 1M context
key_facts.excerpt: Improved Architecture: We propose IndexShare, which reuses the same indexer across every four sparse attention layers, reducing per-token FLOPs by 2.9x at a 1M context length. We also improve GLM-5.2's MTP layer for speculative decoding, increasing the acceptance length by up to 20%

key_facts.fact: API pricing is $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens; enterprise subscriptions start at $12.60/month
key_facts.excerpt: Available immediately on Hugging Face, the Z.ai API, and more than 20 third-party coding environments, the model boasts a highly stable 1-million-token context window alongside enterprise subscription tiers starting at just $12.60 per month... GLM-5.2 API access is priced at $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens

key_facts.fact: The 1M-token context is a 5x jump over GLM-5.1's 200K limit, putting GLM-5.2 among the rare open-weight models that can process book-length inputs in one pass
key_facts.excerpt: GLM-5.2's predecessor, GLM-5.1, topped out at 200,000 tokens. This new version handles five times that amount, putting it in rare company among open-weight models that can actually process book-length inputs in a single pass.

stories.headline: Sensor Tower: ChatGPT's global AI assistant share falls below 50% for first time

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT's global market share fell to 46.4% by end of May after Gemini rose to 27.7% and Claude to 10.3%; Grok, Perplexity, DeepSeek and Meta AI each have under 5%
key_facts.excerpt: Until January, ChatGPT commanded over 50% market share, but by May's end, it had fallen to 46.4% thanks to the rise of Gemini (27.7%) and Claude (10.3%). Other assistants, including Grok, Perplexity, DeepSeek, and Meta AI, have less than 5% market share.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT became the fastest mobile app ever to reach 1 billion monthly active users in May 2026, hitting the milestone in three years, faster than TikTok, YouTube, or Instagram
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT continues to lead the AI Assistant market, becoming the fastest mobile app ever to reach one billion monthly active users in May 2026. The app achieved the milestone in just three years—faster than TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT has 1.1B+ monthly users, followed by Gemini with 662M and Claude with 245M
key_facts.excerpt: The chatbot still remains the most popular AI assistant worldwide with over 1.1 billion monthly users, followed by Gemini with 662 million and Claude with 245 million.

key_facts.fact: Claude's True Audience was up 452% YoY in May and its US market share rose from 4.4% to nearly 14% over the same period
key_facts.excerpt: Claude has emerged as the fastest-growing challenger in 2026, with True Audience up 452% YoY in May and US market share rising from 4.4% to nearly 14% over the same period.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's deal with the US Department of War triggered a spike in ChatGPT uninstalls of ~200% above the app's average during the week of March 9-15; Claude logged more daily downloads than ChatGPT from March 1-5
key_facts.excerpt: In the United States, ChatGPT uninstalls surged following OpenAI's agreement with the Department of War, peaking at roughly 200% above the app's average during the week of March 9-15. Many users who uninstalled ChatGPT appeared to switch to Claude, following Anthropic's decision to decline a partnership with the Pentagon. Claude recorded more daily downloads than ChatGPT from March 1-5.

key_facts.fact: Global time spent on generative AI apps is projected to more than double YoY in H1 2026, from 17.2B hours in H1 2025 to 36B hours
key_facts.excerpt: The report reveals that global time spent on Generative AI apps is projected to more than double year-over-year (YoY) in H1 2026, climbing from 17.2 billion hours in H1 2025 to 36 billion hours in H1 2026.

stories.headline: CuspAI raises $400M at $2.6B valuation backed by Bezos to discover new materials with AI

key_facts.fact: Cambridge-based CuspAI is raising at least $400M from Bezos Expeditions and Kleiner Perkins, valuing the company at $2.6B — more than quadruple its $520M valuation in September 2025
key_facts.excerpt: CuspAI, a UK startup using AI to discover new materials, is raising $400m from investors including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos's family office Bezos Expeditions and Kleiner Perkins. The round would value the company at $2.6bn, more than quadruple what it was worth in September last year, when it raised $100m

key_facts.fact: Term sheets have been signed but the deal has not yet closed, per the Financial Times
key_facts.excerpt: Term sheets have been signed but the deal has not yet closed, per the same report.

key_facts.fact: CuspAI was founded in 2024 by Chad Edwards and Max Welling, building a 'search engine for materials' that uses generative AI to design molecules with desired properties, then validates them via simulation
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2024, CuspAI describes itself as a frontier AI company specialising in generative AI and molecular simulation to accelerate the discovery of breakthrough materials for industrial applications across semiconductors, energy, and climate.

key_facts.fact: Yann LeCun (former Meta chief AI scientist, founder of AMI Labs) and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton sit on the board; existing backers include Lightspeed, Northzone, NEA and Temasek
key_facts.excerpt: The company also has Yann LeCun, previously Meta's chief AI scientist and now founder of world models startup AMI Labs, and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton, on its board. CuspAI's existing backers include Lightspeed Venture Partners, Northzone, NEA and Temasek.

key_facts.fact: CuspAI was named in the UK government's AI for Science strategy and was among the first companies granted significant access to the Isambard AI supercomputer; Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has cited it as a UK startup to watch
key_facts.excerpt: CuspAI was one of the frontier AI companies named in the UK government's AI for Science strategy and was among the first to gain significant access to the Isambard AI supercomputer. Jensen Huang has also cited the company as one of the UK startups to watch

stories.headline: Trump administration rejects UK plea for carve-out from Anthropic Fable/Mythos export ban

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration ruled out granting allied nations access to Anthropic's most advanced AI models, telling officials a G7 exemption would be 'completely illogical'
key_facts.excerpt: Amid the ongoing G7 summit, the Trump administration has reportedly ruled out granting allied nations access to Anthropic's most advanced AI models, maintaining restrictions imposed last week over national security concerns... granting exemptions to any G7 ally would be 'completely illogical.'

key_facts.fact: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer requested a carve-out so British nationals and companies could regain access to Mythos 5 and Fable 5; a senior White House official told the New York Post 'We can't have frontier models running amok'
key_facts.excerpt: Keir Starmer requested a carveout from the embargo on Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models for British nationals and companies - and was denied. A senior White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told the New York Post: 'We can't have frontier models running amok'.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has suspended Fable 5 and Mythos 5 globally to comply with the US Commerce Department export controls served on Friday
key_facts.excerpt: The export order, served on Friday by the US Commerce Department, forced Anthropic to disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for every user worldwide to stay compliant.

key_facts.fact: US officials raised concerns that Anthropic's Fable 5 could be 'jailbroken' to unlock the more powerful cyber-security capabilities of Mythos 5; Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick joined parts of the Anthropic talks remotely from the G7 summit
key_facts.excerpt: The restrictions were introduced after US officials raised concerns that Anthropic's recently released Fable 5 model could potentially be 'jailbroken', allowing users to unlock the more powerful cyber-security capabilities of Mythos 5. US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reportedly joined parts of the talks remotely from the G7 summit in France

key_facts.fact: Insiders expect Trump will ultimately roll back the restriction globally rather than grant the UK a bespoke exemption; Anthropic and the administration continue direct negotiations
key_facts.excerpt: Insiders expect Trump will ultimately strike a deal that rolls back the restriction for everyone rather than grant Britain a bespoke exemption.

stories.headline: Former Qwen lead Lin Junyang's stealth AI lab closes hundreds of millions at $2B valuation

key_facts.fact: Junyang Lin, the former lead of Alibaba's Qwen models, raised several hundred million dollars at a ~$2B post-money valuation for a new AI lab focused on world models and embodied intelligence
key_facts.excerpt: Former Alibaba executive and Qwen model leader Justin Lin Junyang (林俊旸) has raised several hundred million dollars for a new AI startup focused on world models and embodied intelligence... The deal gave the company a post-money valuation of about $2 billion despite having no public product, revenue or official website.

key_facts.fact: Gaorong Capital and Sequoia China (HongShan) each invested roughly $100M as lead investors; Tencent followed with $20M
key_facts.excerpt: The two people familiar with the matter said that this completed round of financing was led by Gao Rong Venture Capital and Sequoia China. Each of these two venture capital institutions invested $100 million (approximately RMB 675 million). In addition, Tencent invested $20 million (approximately RMB 135 million) in this round of financing.

key_facts.fact: Tencent's investment continues a strategy of backing multiple model developers beyond its in-house Hunyuan model — it has previously backed Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Zhipu AI, and is reportedly joining DeepSeek's latest round
key_facts.excerpt: According to The Information, Tencent has previously invested in Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Zhipu AI, and is reportedly participating in the latest financing round for DeepSeek.

key_facts.fact: Lin Junyang joined Alibaba's DAMO Academy in 2019 and led the Qwen family of LLMs after the Tongyi Lab was set up in 2022, becoming one of the youngest P10 technical leads at Alibaba
key_facts.excerpt: In 2019, Lin Junyang joined the Intelligent Computing Laboratory of Alibaba's DAMO Academy... at the end of 2022, Alibaba integrated relevant AI teams into the Tongyi Laboratory system. He was appointed as the technical head of the Tongyi Qianwen (Qwen) series of large models and became one of the youngest P10-level technical heads in the Alibaba system.

key_facts.fact: The new lab is already preparing for a follow-on fundraising round immediately after closing this one
key_facts.excerpt: The team is already preparing for a follow-on fundraising round, the report said.
